articles.title: Did someone wearing Meta Glasses film you today? Are you sure?
articles.summary: People say they’ve been secretly filmed in their own home, at concerts and at work. Are the wildly popular smartglasses the final nail in the coffin of personal privacy? “I’ve had one person who told me that their intentions were creepy,” a man tells me over a video call, on condition of anonymity.
body: The man I’m talking to runs a business called Ghost Metas. He’s one of hundreds of vendors, easily discoverable online, who specialise in disabling the flashing LED light embedded in Meta’s smartglasses that blinks when wearers capture photos, videos and audio. After Ghost Metas disables the LED, it’s impossible for someone to know they’re being filmed.

He flips his camera over to show me his work bench, revealing painter’s tape, a drill, a hole puncher, a dental pick and a tube of resin. He says he’s worked on about 100 pairs of glasses, and that one pair only takes him about 15 to 20 minutes.
“In public, I don’t think we have privacy any more, period,” he says, when I ask whether what he’s doing feels wrong. “My argument is if you’re really worried about your privacy, don’t go outside.”
points: People say they’ve been secretly filmed in their own home, at concerts and at work.

articles.title: Hogging weights, loud grunting and sweaty benches: 11 gym dos and don’ts from fitness experts
articles.summary: Here’s what professionals have to say about good workout etiquette, from using equipment to being on your phone. I like to think of myself as a fairly laid-back person. Other people’s behavior is not my business. There is one notable exception: my gym nemesis.
body: He brings his computer to the gym and takes work conference calls at full volume. He has four to six pairs of dumbbells around him at all times – then doesn’t put them away. Intellectually I understand he is a fragile, flawed human like the rest of us, but in my gut I sometimes wonder if he arrived here from another galaxy.

Life is full of unspoken rules, and the gym is no different. The heavy weights, sweaty people and mysterious machines can make it daunting to figure out how to behave. So we asked fitness experts for their thoughts on gym etiquette – their biggest pet peeves as well as the behaviors that might seem intimidating, but are actually fine.

Good gym etiquette is less about following a long list of rules than it is simple respect, says Mathew Forzaglia, a fitness professional and educator. “Respect the equipment, respect other people’s time and space, and respect the shared environment,” he says.

Whether it’s leaving a bench covered in your sweat, or not re-racking weights after you use them, failing to clean and reset equipment after you use it is not only a hygiene issue, it’s potentially unsafe.

articles.title: Stephen Libby on fashion: a summer wedding is no time for your funeral suit – have fun with colour
articles.summary: The Traitors star gives his tips on how to shine at a wedding – from mismatching jacket and trousers to rocking a man bag. For a long time, I didn’t enjoy going to weddings. It wasn’t the celebration or the party that put me off – it was the clothes.
body: Wedding guest attire for women is a whole micro-industry these days. But men are still stuck in the dark ages. It’s all grey, navy and black suits. I often see men wearing the same sort of suit they might wear to a funeral. What kind of message is that sending? It’s high time we got to experiment because a wedding is a celebration of love. You don’t want to look like you’re in mourning.

If it’s a summer wedding – and given it’s August, this is why we’re here – then suit-wise you should absolutely go for a relaxed cut and a different colour than you’re used to. Try approaching things as if you were going to southern Puglia for a location wedding. Maybe a pale blue or green suit, or a jacket with a dropped shoulder and a wider leg. Loose clothing is also going to keep you cooler, so if anyone raises an eyebrow you can always just blame the heat.

articles.title: Björk, an Eclipse, and 40 Years of Icelandic Underground Music
articles.summary: Björk’s eclipse rave was more than a party: It was a celebration of the Icelandic label and creative community that helped shape the country’s singular music scene.
body: I was warned that the light change right before totality would feel the strangest. As I looked up at the cloud-strewn Icelandic sky, the crowd pulsing around me, it was as if the world had transformed into a film noir—our upturned faces suddenly cast in washed-out shades of grey.
Then, for a minute, everything slipped into pitch-black darkness. In those few moments, strangers hugged; I cried and laughed simultaneously; and one person yelled “You’re doing great, moon!”
When the moon crossed between the Earth and the sun on August 12, we couldn’t see the total solar eclipse —but we could feel it. We were standing in the moon’s shadow.

There were no groans, complaints, or frowns, in part because our anticipation was two-fold. The dark green weather forecast (indicating the heaviest level of cloud coverage) had sent many of the more devoted eclipse chasers north, chasing clear skies. But thousands of us chose to remain in Víðistaðatún, a sculpture park strewn with massive lava rocks in Hafnarfjörður about six miles from Downtown Reykjavik, for Echolalia, a one-day rave headlined by Björk, arguably Iceland’s most famous musician.
points: Björk’s eclipse rave was more than a party: It was a celebration of the Icelandic label and creative community that helped shape the country’s singular music scene.

articles.title: I Finally Tried A313, France’s Cult-Favorite Retinoid
articles.summary: A313 is one of the most popular French pharmacy products, but does it actually live up to the hype? Here, Vogue explores the retinoid’s popularity and gets the inside scoop on its benefits.
body: Rarely do I succumb to a TikTok beauty product recommendation. But the A313 Vitamin A pomade has been in my orbit long before social media claimed it; for years many of my US editor friends and go-to beauty experts have raved about its effects on skin. So now that my algorithm is being fed an endless amount of French pharmacy hauls, I finally made it a goal to brave the Paris summer crowds at the Pharmacie Citypharma on 26 Rue du Four to buy my first tube.

To my surprise, the French don’t actually consider A313 an anti-aging skincare product. As Natacha Bonjout, French pharmacist and founder of Bonjout Beauty, explains, it has been used for decades as more of a functional medicine. “The reality is more nuanced,” Bonjout says. “The product is old, but the story around it is new.”

But thanks to America’s fascination with French pharmacy culture, the product has gotten a new life thanks to social media. Whether intended or not, it has become the skin-care symbol of French beauty. “It feels like an insider secret,” she goes on to say. “So I don’t think [US] consumers are only buying A313; they’re buying into the idea of French pharmacy.”
points: A313 is one of the most popular French pharmacy products, but does it actually live up to the hype?

articles.title: These Vogue-Approved Totes Are the Best Work Bags for Women
articles.summary: Shop Vogue’s guide to the best work bags for women, from classic canvas carryalls to sleek leather totes, from L.L. Bean, Toteme, The Row, Khaite, and more.
body: The best work bags for women should always meet two criteria: function and style. When searching for your own, ask yourself, is it durable? Will it be sizable enough to fit all of your essentials—laptop, notebooks, planners, wallet, keys, and beauty staples? Is it lightweight and comfortable enough to wear over your shoulders (and jacket!), especially during a daily commute?

I’ve learned the hard way—purchasing work bags that are too heavy to start with, only to find them almost impossible to lug around once filled. Not a smart investment, and it put me back straight back to square one.
The one silver lining of all my trial and error? I can now intuit which work bags will check my proverbial boxes of style and durability; of spaciousness and lightweight portability.

articles.title: 7 Vacation Outfits to Try, Inspired by Celebrities
articles.summary: Shop our favorite celebrity vacation outfits that will take you from swimming in the Mediterranean to strolling the streets of Paris or Rome, all with stylish flair.
body: With a few more weeks of summer left (let’s not forget, the last official day is September 22!), end-of-season vacations are top of mind, especially as we near Labor Day weekend. If you’re looking for a little inspiration on what to pack and wear, let these celebrity vacation outfits guide the way. From seaside escapes to urban adventures, these looks offer plenty of fresh ideas for making the most of the final weeks of summer.

If a Mediterranean destination is calling, or any beach getaway for that matter, look to playful prints for your next vacation look. Whether you take cues from supermodel Vittoria Ceretti’s bold, bright cabana stripes or Laura Harrier’s polka-dot prints in Saint-Tropez, leaning into retro patterns is an easy way to give your holiday wardrobe a timeless, nostalgic feel.

You can also go the summer-in-the-city route, like Gigi Hadid, who wore a white tank top and lace-trimmed slip skirt while dining out in Paris. Finishing with black flip-flops and a polka-dot shoulder bag, it’s a lesson in how a few well-chosen accessories can make even the simplest outfit feel vacation-ready.
